note: A stand-in for the route's first section until the Khumbu Icefall (#26) brings the real ground and the knowledge base's numbers: a made-up line shaped like the Icefall, with made-up speeds, slip chances, the speed a hazard knocks a climber down at, and stretches of it under a serac, over a hidden crevasse and under an avalanche slope, in clear weather. Nothing here is a fact. Every sloping segment is a Pythagorean triple, so the distances along the ground, which the ropes, the ladders and the climbers are laid by, are whole metres: the corners are at 0, 20, 45, 58, 63, 67, 72, 84, 99, 102, 117, 130, 155, 172, 182, 190, 198, 223, 240, 265, 278, 299, 324, 344 and 364 m along it. The altitude of its ends and the clock's start are made up too; the ends are 12 times the drawn rise apart, since every section is drawn at 1/time.compression (docs/conventions/slope-physics.md → The slope).
